items.description: Python arbitrary-precision integers are represented only inside the declared signed-int64 domain.
items.containment: 14A accepts exact integer-like operands only; out-of-domain or incomplete representation evidence rejects, and no checked-arithmetic or big-integer runtime is introduced.
items.next_decision: Seal the existing signed-int64 boundary with divmod obligation fixtures; broader integer semantics remain a separately approved future evaluation.

items.description: C division and remainder are undefined for zero and INT64_MIN divided by negative one, while Python has defined failure or arbitrary-precision behavior.
items.containment: The divisor must be a directly proved existing-lowerable literal in [-9223372036854775807, -2] or [1, 9223372036854775807] before either frozen helper can be selected; 0, -1, and INT64_MIN reject and no runtime failure channel exists.
items.next_decision: Implement and independently validate the exact literal proof, then seal it with boundary and rejection fixtures.

items.description: General Python exceptions, arithmetic failures, raise/assert, and unwinding have no approved C runtime representation.
items.containment: All exception-bearing or runtime-failure-dependent forms reject; 14A closes its preconditions statically and cannot emit a hidden failure path.
items.next_decision: A separately approved exception mini-phase must specify propagation, cleanup, ownership, traceback limits, and cancellation before any implementation.

items.description: Effectful calls needing eager temporaries inside later Boolean or chained-comparison operands can violate Python conditional evaluation.
items.containment: Existing PYC2950/PYC2951 boundaries reject the affected forms; 14A adds no conditional placement rule.
items.next_decision: Evaluate conditional temporary regions as their own mini-phase after 14A is sealed.

items.description: Direct and mutual recursion lack a separately budgeted resource and termination contract.
items.containment: The closed call graph continues to detect and reject recursion; 14A does not change call eligibility.
items.next_decision: Retain clean rejection unless a separately approved bounded recursion contract is proposed.

items.description: Formatting, concatenation, allocation, encoding failure, and owned string lifetime are outside the borrowed-literal string boundary.
items.containment: Only the existing immutable UTF-8 literal and borrowed const-char-pointer boundary remains eligible; f-strings and advanced string operations reject.
items.next_decision: Evaluate f-strings and advanced string operations independently with representation, allocation, cleanup, and failure budgets.

items.description: Defaults, keyword arguments, keyword-only parameters, variadics, and unpacking require richer deterministic binding and evaluation rules.
items.containment: Only exact positional calls and structural record construction remain accepted; every expanded call shape rejects before planning.
items.next_decision: Evaluate direct keyword binding first in an independent post-14A mini-phase; do not bundle defaults, variadics, or unpacking.

items.description: Comprehensions and pattern matching introduce hidden scopes, conditional binding, iteration, and failure-sensitive control flow.
items.containment: All comprehension nodes and Match forms remain unsupported; they cannot reuse container or assignment support by analogy.
items.next_decision: Give each family a separate feasibility classification after 14A; acceptance of one will not authorize the other.

items.description: Context managers and finally regions require exact cleanup ordering across normal, failure, return, break, continue, and cancellation paths.
items.containment: With/async-with and try/finally remain unsupported; no implicit cleanup stack or exit protocol exists.
items.next_decision: Do not open until an exception and cleanup-region architecture is separately approved.

items.description: Generators and async syntax require suspension state, retained locals, resumption, ownership, cancellation, and scheduler boundaries.
items.containment: Yield, yield-from, await, async functions, async iteration, and async context managers reject; no state machine or scheduler surface exists.
items.next_decision: Require a dedicated state-machine architecture and resource model before any feature implementation.

items.description: Closures, nonlocal capture, lambdas, and decorators require environment objects or import-time callable transformation.
items.containment: Nested functions, nonlocal, lambda values, decorators, and indirect callables remain cleanly rejected; no environment allocation is emitted.
items.next_decision: Evaluate lexical closure representation independently; decorators remain deferred unless their execution timing is separately modeled.

items.description: Destructuring, starred assignment, assignment expressions, global/nonlocal mutation, and deletion can alter binding lifetime and control-visible state.
items.containment: Existing direct single-name assignments remain the boundary; these forms reject and cannot be inferred from tuple, container, or record support.
items.next_decision: Evaluate fixed tuple destructuring and a narrow assignment-expression profile separately after 14A; defer global, nonlocal, and deletion.

items.description: Sets, dynamic operations, comprehensions, slicing, mutation, aliasing, and escape exceed fixed local container ownership.
items.containment: The Phase 11 fixed-capacity, direct-local, immutable-use profile remains exact; all advanced operations reject.
items.next_decision: Any evaluated operation receives its own capacity, representation, ownership, failure, and helper decision.

items.description: General classes require identity, inheritance, dispatch, descriptors, mutation, allocation, aliasing, and lifecycle semantics absent from static records.
items.containment: Only the sealed Phase 13 immutable automatic static-record grammar is supported; every neighboring object-model form has stable rejection.
items.next_decision: Remain deferred unless a future roadmap explicitly reopens the general object model with a complete runtime architecture.
